text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers. LES ECHOS

-- Insurer UAP expected to post 6 to 7 billion franc loss for 1996, wich should not weigh on Axa and BNP results. Axa -UAP considers selling UAP stakes in Elf Aquitaine , Eurafrance, Gaz et Eaux, BNP .
-- President Jacques Chirac calls for a national debate on education and possible reform.
-- President Jacques Chirac calls for a reduced, 5.6 percent value-added tax for multimedia products and services.
-- EU authorities about to reject French plan for state help to the French textile sector on grounds that it distorts fair competition in a single European market.
-- French stockmarkets association chairman Jean-Francois Theodore in an interview calls for a European stockmarket structure which he says could take the shape of a consortium such as Airbus.
-- A planned acquisition of Credit du Nord by Societe Generale may be signed today, is expected to boost Societe Generale's growth.
-- Boards of Thomson SA and Thomson-CSF to meet this morning for a presentation of a book of terms and conditions ahead of a privatisation through private placement of Thomson-CSF.
-- Renault workers from European countries to demonstrate in Paris area against planned plant shut-down in Belgium and restructuring.
